title: Asynchronous code fails to use session state on Streamlit Cloud while it works locally
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The error appears while running an asynchronous chronometer/stopwatch controlled by a Streamlit interface.
The session state variables are failed to be used on the deployed version on Streamlit Cloud, while the same code works fine locally.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6818)

```Python
import asyncio
import time

import streamlit as st


async def run_chronometer(container):
    while st.session_state["chrono_running"]:
        st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"] = time.time()
        run_time = (
            st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"] - st.session_state["chrono_start_ts"]
        )
        container.subheader(f"{run_time:.2f}")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)


def init_chrono():
    st.session_state["chrono_running"] = False
    st.session_state["chrono_start_ts"] = None
    st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"] = None


if "chrono_running" not in st.session_state:
    init_chrono()

st.header("Chronometer")
col1_run, col2_run = st.columns(2)
container = st.empty()
col1_save, col2_save = st.columns(2)

# buttons to run chronometer
with col1_run:
    if st.button("Start", use_container_width=True):
        st.session_state["chrono_start_ts"] = time.time()
        st.session_state["chrono_running"] = True
        st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"] = None

with col2_run:
    if st.button("Stop", use_container_width=True):
        st.session_state["chrono_running"] = False

# fill container when chrono is not running
if not st.session_state["chrono_running"]:
    if not st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"]:
        container.subheader(f"{0.0:.2f}")
    else:
        run_time = round(
            st.session_state.chrono_stop_ts - st.session_state.chrono_start_ts, 2
        )
        container.subheader(f"{run_time:.2f}")

# buttons to save chronometer result
with col1_save:
    if st.button(
        "Save",
        disabled=(not st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"]),
        use_container_width=True,
    ):
        st.write("Saved time:", run_time)

with col2_save:
    if st.button(
        "Delete",
        disabled=(not st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"]),
        use_container_width=True,
    ):
        init_chrono()
        st.experimental_rerun()

# run chronometer asynchronously
asyncio.run(run_chronometer(container))
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Go to the [deployed version](https://chronometer-error.streamlit.app/).

Then follow these steps:
- Click on "Start" button
- Click on "Stop" button
- Click on "Save" or "Delete" buttons
- Click on "Start" button again
- Click on "Stop" button again

### Expected Behavior

When you click "Start" the app displays the running time, when you click "Stop" it shows the time that passed from start to stop.

### Current Behavior

Running the code locally works fine.

Running the deployed app, the stop time is failed to be captured (showing 0) and the following error message pops up:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):

  File "/home/appuser/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py", line 565, in _run_script

    exec(code, module.__dict__)

  File "/app/streamlit-chronometer/chronometer.py", line 78, in <module>

    asyncio.run(run_chronometer(container))

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/asyncio/runners.py", line 44, in run

    return loop.run_until_complete(main)

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/asyncio/base_events.py", line 649, in run_until_complete

    return future.result()

  File "/app/streamlit-chronometer/chronometer.py", line 14, in run_chronometer

    while st.session_state["chrono_running"] and run_time < MAX_TIME - TIMESTEP_REAL:

  File "/home/appuser/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state_proxy.py", line 90, in __getitem__

    return get_session_state()[key]

  File "/home/appuser/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/safe_session_state.py", line 104, in __getitem__

    raise KeyError(key)
KeyError: 'chrono_running'
```

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.19
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Google Chrome
- Virtual environment: conda


### Additional Information

The repository with the full reproducible code and the used `requirements.txt` file can be found [here](https://github.com/tommitassi/streamlit-chronometer).

If you try to use `streamlit==1.20+`, you would obtain the same error locally as well. I found out this is due to the `fastReruns` default value which has become `true` in these releases. If you overwrite the value to `false` within `.streamlit/config.toml` file, you would solve the problem locally but it will persist on the deployed version. Using `streamlit==1.19` overcomes this problem.

title: Compact layout and compact widgets to get the most from the available screen space
body:
### Problem

Streamlit's overall layout and individual components are quite wasteful with screen space – there is a lot of white space everywhere.

This is great for simple apps for casual users, but it creates a usability problem in applications where you want to give power users many options to tweak without scrolling away from the main visualization or data table, or just provide a high information density on one screen. Tabs and expanders offer some relief, but they limit what you can have on the screen at one time. 

Applications like Tableau, R shiny, and the ubiquitous Excel based tools have a much higher information density than Streamlit apps. If Streamlit aims to be an alternative to those applications in "power user" scenarios (think finance, BI, scientific visualization,...), it needs the capability to present UIs with higher density.

Examples of very generous use of space:

* large font size in widgets like `selectbox`, `multiselect`, `slider`, and others
* large size of the main widget "box" in `selectbox`, `number_input` and others
* `file_uploader` is huge!
* tables aren't particularly compact either
* lots of white space between components
* whitespace on top of screen (see #6336, but the issue here is wider) 

Things that go in the right direction:

* wide mode
* horizontal layout for `radio`
* the new options for label placement, including the option to ditch the labels altogether
* sometimes it just helps to zoom out in the browser, but of course that is not a solution

### Solution

**MVP:** What's the smallest possible solution that would get 80% of the problem out of the way?

* provide a "compact layout" and/or "small fonts"  option for the chunkiest controls; see examples above
* solve #6336
* provide an alternative style option that reduces whitespace between components

**Possible additions:** What are other things that could be added to the MVP over time to make it better?

* more options for label placement, for example left of control (I realize, though, that this probably generates ugly alignment problem; maybe there could be some sort of "form table", where labels are in one column and controls next to it)
* just more layout options in general – grids, complex multicolumn alignment – would help to make use of screen space

### Additional context

Where I work, I'm heavily advertising replacing insanely complex Excel-tools with proper Python code + Streamlit UI. While there is a lot of buy-in for replacing the actual logic with Python, I frequently meet resistance when it comes to the UI. As much as I dislike Excel – you can get a lot of control on a single screen there. I have seem similar arguments when it comes to pitching Streamlit + Altair as an alternative to Tableau.

This issue was created as suggested in the forum [on this thread](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/compact-layout-and-components/45639/3).

title: st.chat_input drops submission after placeholder text change
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

This may be a known issue with placeholders, although I didn't see this in the docs or an existing issue. (If this is a duplicate, my apologies!)

If the placeholder text is changed in an [st.chat_input](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/chat/st.chat_input) conditional on state that is updated by the chat_input submission, the next submission will be silently dropped (it _will_ rerun the app, as expected)

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if "word" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["word"] = ""

new_word = st.chat_input("Enter word" if st.session_state.word == "" else "Update word")
if new_word:
    st.session_state.word = new_word
    print(new_word)
st.write(f"Word: {st.session_state.word}")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Enter a string in the chat_input and submit it.
2. Enter a second string in the chat_input and submit it.

### Expected Behavior

For example entries "1", "2", "3", expected stdout output is:
```
1
2
3
```

### Current Behavior

The actual output is:
```
1
3
```

The second input will be dropped unless the app is rerun. Note that providing a key to the chat_input doesn't help, and that the placeholder text follows expected behavior (i.e. it won't update from "Enter word" to "Update word" until after the second submission).

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.24.0
- Python version: 3.10.11
- Operating System: MacOs 13.4
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

This issue has an easy workaround: don't use the return value to update state, and instead use a callback. This also prevents "stale" placeholder text when the state has been updated but the app hasn't been re-run.

For example:
```python
import streamlit as st

def chat_input_submit():
    st.session_state.word = st.session_state.chat_input_key

if "word" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["word"] = ""

st.write(f"Word: {st.session_state.word}")
st.chat_input("Enter word" if st.session_state.word == "" else "Update word", key="chat_input_key", on_submit=chat_input_submit)
```

def _fix_related_model(self) -> None:
    for related in get_candidate_relations_to_delete(self._meta):
        related: ManyToOneRel
        field: ForeignKey = related.field


        model = self._meta.model

        def correct_polymorphic(rel_model: AbstractBaseModel) -> AbstractBaseModel:
            """
            with django-polymorphic, model is always the leaf class, but rel_model is sometimes the base one
            """
            fixed = self._meta.model
            while rel_model._meta.label != fixed._meta.label:
                fixed = next(iter(fixed._meta.parents))
            return fixed

        rmod = correct_polymorphic(related.model)
        if related.model is not rmod:
            related.model = rmod
        fmod = correct_polymorphic(field.related_model)
        if field.related_model is not fmod:
            field.related_model = fmod

```

title: st.progress with recurring timer, key and callback
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Setting the st.progress in a loop when doing something slow is certainly intuitive, but how about giving the slider a timer, a callback and a key. 

The timer could also be a new standalone invisible widget, e.g., st.timer(interval=1000, callback=my_callback, ...)

This would allow for example to scan an API endpoint for progress in the callback ,and set the progress value there. This would make more sense if you won't run the entire python script on any change in the frontend. I think you could still use your paradigm for interactive widgets, where the user is giving some input through the frontend, but for a progress update, which is a "pure output" widget, you could use a different paradigm (i.e. the python script won't be re-run). 

I think this new paradigm (special case for pure output widgets) won't overcomplicate your nice model, you will just have to explain that the "pure output" and "input" widgets behave differently. 

Without this, you either have stay in a loop updating the progress, thus blocking the python script (which has as a side effect that other widgets are dimmed), or to use st.experimental_rerun with some st.session_state and implement state-machines (certainly doable, but messier). 

Thank you for your time, and keep going with your great framework! I'm a big fan!

### Why?

Think about a REST API which provides an endpoint for starting a long task, and a second endpoint where you can get the progress of the long running task. 

Without a timer, you either have stay in a loop querying the API and updating the progress, thus blocking the python script (which has as a side effect that it dims other output), or to use st.experimental_rerun with some st.session_state and implement state-machines (certainly doable, but messier). 

### How?

st.timer(interval=1000, callback=on_tick)

Ideally no python script rerun on timer callback or progress update.

title: Add form validation to make form fields required
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit currently has no built-in form validation to prevent a form from being submitted when one or more of he required fields is not populated or has invalid data. Adding a manual check that gets executed on form submit button click is not ideal from a user experience point of view, because this means either the entire form will be cleared even when a required field is not correctly populated when the form's clear_on_submit property is set as True, or the form fields will still carry the entered values even when the form is successfully submitted if the form's clear_on_submit property is set as False.

### Why?

If a form is submitted with all necessary fields populated, ideally I would want the form to be cleared upon submission and hence would want clear_on_submit set to True. When, however, a necessary field is left empty I would indeed want the already populated fields to retain the provided input rather than being cleared.

I could not make things work with a form but wrote a workaround that does not use a form as follows: I created input fields (not inside a form), created state vars assigned to keys of input fields, added a standard button, created a function to reset the state variables to be called from within the on_click function of the button only when all compulsory fields are populated.

However, I do think this is way too much work for a simple form validation, which is pretty fundamental feature built into any web framework that I’ve ever worked with (I do recognise that Streamlit probably does not aim to become an all-purpose web framework but still), and in my humble opinion, make it difficult for Streamlit to be adopted by a wider user base.

### How?

Adding a `required` property to form input fields might be a possible solution. 

### Additional Context

This issue was discussed at [https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/make-input-fields-required-using-st-form/30822](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/make-input-fields-required-using-st-form/30822)

title: Built-In run_query with session_state
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

In conjunction with the st.experimental_connection feature, it would be nice to have sql queries that take one line of code. In addition, these queries could have an option to use existing results in a session_state if the query errors out

### Why?

These three components - the connection, the query and the error handling - all seem built out already and it would be nice to have them efficiently together as a built-in method

### How?

I'm not sure if the st.experimental_connection is included in the new method - it seems like that might be a separate first step and then step two would be something like st.run_query_with_handling(query: str, client: client, use_state: bool = True, state_name: str = None) to pull the data (client is a made-up type here, it would probably be a generic connection type defined in the class)

For st.run_query_with_handling, there could be two steps:

1. From https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/tutorials/databases/bigquery - as an example. Create a connection based on the conn_type and pull data with the query:

```
# Perform query.
# Uses st.cache_data to only rerun when the query changes or after 10 min.
@st.cache_data(ttl=600)
def run_query(query, client):
    query_job = client.query(query)
    rows_raw = query_job.result()
    # Convert to list of dicts. Required for st.cache_data to hash the return value.
    rows = [dict(row) for row in rows_raw]
    return rows
```

2. Create a wrapper that attempts the run #1 but uses existing results in st.session_state if use_state=True, else throws an error

```
def run_query_with_handling(query, client, use_state, state_name):
    try:
        output_data = query_func(query, client)
        st.session_state[state_name] = output_data
    except Exception as e:
        if state_name in st.session_state and use_state:
            log_str = (f"Unable to pull the most recent {state_name}, "
                       f"using data from the previous pull instead. "
                       f"Please check your internet connection and try "
                       f"again if necessary.\n"
                       f"Error: {e}")
            st.sidebar.warning(log_str)
            output_data = st.session_state[state_name]
        else:
            log_str = (f"*******************Error*******************\n"
                       f"Could not get {state_name}. If another error is "
                       f"not present, either {state_name} doesn't exist in "
                       f"the database or the connection is broken.\n"
                       f"Error: {e}")
            st.error(log_str)
    return output_data
```

Note that the output (st.sidebar.warning and st.error) seem like nice communication with the user, but could be optional or done in another way.

title: Callback state change issue on date widget
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I tried searching for comparable issues using: ```is:issue is:open callback -label:type:enhancement``` but I could not find a direct match..

The issue I'm running into is that the callback function on the datepicker widget fires when the state is set programmatically _using `datetime`_. So pretty much all the input fields in the datepicker widget accept `datetime` and implicitly cast them to `date`. This is fine behavior and just works. But when setting the underlying state it gives a problem, when setting the underlying state to a date programmatically the callback does not fire. This is correct behavior in my opinion. The callback should only fire when actually using the input widget. But when setting the underlying state to a `datetime`, it's cast to a `date` _and_ the callback fires. I'm guessing it's caused by the cast?

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7216)

```Python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st


def updated():
    if st.session_state.get("thingy"):
        st.write(st.session_state.thingy)
    st.write(dt.datetime.now())


def update_value():
    # Uncomment/comment the below lines to go from correct to incorrect behavior
    # st.session_state.thingy = st.session_state.thingy + dt.timedelta(days=1)
    st.session_state.thingy = dt.datetime.now()


def main():
    st.title("reproducible")
    st.date_input("thingy", key="thingy", on_change=updated)
    st.button("update thingy", on_click=update_value)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Click the button. The callback fires even though the user does not click the datepicker.

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the callback not to fire when setting it's state programmatically.. This is indeed the behaviour when setting the state to a `date` but when setting it to a `datetime` the callback fires.

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.25.0
- Python version: 3.11.0
- Operating System: Linux Mint 21.1
- Browser: Firefox 116.0.3


### Additional Information

_No response_

### Summary

In my Streamlit application, I have implemented a feature where users can upload a text file. The workflow involves hitting a "preprocessing" button, which triggers the preprocessing of the uploaded text, and then displaying the preprocessed output. Afterward, I use this preprocessed output as input for an ML model prediction by hitting the "ML prediction" button, which subsequently displays the predictions.

I have implemented session state to store the value of preprocessing so that I can pass it to the ML model prediction step. However, I've encountered an issue where, when I upload a new file, the preprocessing output of the old file still persists alongside the new output. This behavior is unexpected, as I would expect the preprocessing output to be cleared when a new file is uploaded.

I am initialising session state still it doesnt work:

    if "preprocessed_data" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.preprocessed_data = None
    if "anomaly_output" not in st.session_state:

                ml_output = ml_response.json()["ML model prediction"]
                st.session_state.preprocessed_line_count = len(st.session_state.preprocessed_data)
                st.session_state.anomaly_output = ml_output

title: Widget display value depends on ScriptRunner completing execution of a different page (or not)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using `st.session_state` to pre-set the value of a widget, the widget will sometimes appear to have a blank/0 value that does not match the value returned by the DeltaGenerator function call, and this behavior depends on the user switching from a different Streamlit "page" which did or did not finish running to completion.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# Create a multipage streamlit app

# -- in testpage1.py
import streamlit as st

st.write("Starting")
st.session_state.setdefault("my_widget", "Hello World")
text_value = st.text_input("Enter some text", key="my_widget")
st.write(text_value)
st.button("press to refresh")

# -- in testpage2.py
import streamlit as st
from time import sleep

st.write("starting")
sleep(10)
st.write("finished")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start streamlit with a fresh session on testpage1.py
2. See: "Hello World" in the `my_widget` text_input and "Hello World" printed below it via `st.write`
3. Change the text of the `my_widget` text_input to something else. This step is not strictly required to reproduce the bug but allows you to verify that A) the `.setdefault` call is working as expected and B) that the value has "reset" to the default "Hello World" later on.
4. Navigate to testpage2. Allow 10 seconds for the script to run to completion, so that "Finished" is displayed
5. Navigate back to testpage1.
6. See: "Hello World" in the `my_widget` text_input and "Hello World" printed below it via `st.write`. The input and display state of the widget has been reset to it's default value, and this makes sense, since widgets do not retain their state across page changes.
7. Navigate to testpage2. Before the 10 seconds has elapsed, navigate back to testpage1.
8. See "" (blank) in the `my_widget` text_input, and "Hello World" printed below it via `st.write`. This is unexpected, as the widget visual state does not match the returned value nor the pre-set value that it should have because of the `st.session_state.setdefault` call right before it.
9. Clicking the "press to refresh" button causes the "Hello World" written by `st.write` to disappear (due to the fact that the front-end sends the blank widget state to the backend as part of the ReRun Data for the button press)

### Expected Behavior

Widget visual state on testpage1 reload does not depend on when testpage2 execution was interrupted.

### Summary

If blocking (e.g., HTTP request, sleep) happens after the button click, user inputs on `st.text_area` are not saved on `st.session_state`.
Also, if the blocking function is commented out, inputs on `st.text_area` are saved on `st.session_state` after the button click.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7862)
```Python
import time

import streamlit as st


def set_state(i: int, text: str):
    st.session_state.stage = i
    st.session_state.lines = text.splitlines()


time.sleep(2)
if "stage" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.stage = 0
if st.session_state.stage == 0:
    text = st.text_area("Input your text", height=100)
    st.button(
        "Begin",
        on_click=set_state,
        args=[1, text],
    )
if st.session_state.stage == 1:
    st.title("Your text")
    for i, line in enumerate(st.session_state.lines):
        st.write(f"{i}. {line}")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Input some text on text area
2. Click `Begin` button
3. Only the title is displayed(contents of `st.session_state` are not shown)

Inputs are saved on `st.session_state` and shown after the button click.

title: SQLAchemy dynamic authentication tokens not working with cached connection/data
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello everybody,

I have been dealing with a annoying bug this week, which I will attempt to describe in detail below.

My data is sourced from Azure Synapse Analytics; therefore, authentication with the database occurs via an authentication token. As [SQLAlchemy suggests](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/mssql.html#connecting-to-databases-with-access-tokens), one method to generate dynamic authentication tokens involves setting up an event listener on the engine that adds the credential token to the dialect’s connect call. Specifically for Synapse/SQL Server, this token is passed as an ODBC connection attribute within a data structure [described by Microsoft](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/using-azure-active-directory#authenticating-with-an-access-token).

The first time the app runs, it operates without any problems. However, the issue arises when the query changes. I believe this problem is related to the caching mechanism, which invalidates the event listener, at this point the event listener might be set to a different object; – which is not the one coming from cache?

Because when the query changes I start getting the error "sqlalchemy.exc.DBAPIError: (pyodbc.Error) ('HY000', '[HY000] [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server]SSPI Provider: No Kerberos credentials available (default cache: FILE:/tmp/krb5cc_1000) (851968) (SQLDriverConnect)') (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/dbapi)" which seems to be caused by the fact that SQLAlchemy adds the ";Trusted_Connection=Yes" parameters which should have been removed by the event listener, and probably the lack of authentication token at all.

Below is a minimal Streamlit app that demonstrates the issue:


```python
import struct
from datetime import timedelta
import streamlit as st
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, event
from sqlalchemy.engine import URL

load_dotenv() # Load secrets

# The callback function for the event listener
def provide_token(dialect, conn_rec, cargs, cparams):
    SQL_COPT_SS_ACCESS_TOKEN = 1256  # Connection option for access tokens, as defined in msodbcsql.h
    TOKEN_URL = "https://database.windows.net/.default"  # The token URL for any Azure SQL database
    cargs[0] = cargs[0].replace(
        ";Trusted_Connection=Yes", ""
    )  # remove the "Trusted_Connection" parameter that SQLAlchemy adds
    credentials = DefaultAzureCredential() # It reads app secrets from env
    # Lets build the token and send to the ODBC driver
    raw_token = credentials.get_token(TOKEN_URL).token.encode("utf-16-le")
    token_struct = struct.pack(f"<I{len(raw_token)}s", len(raw_token), raw_token)
    cparams["attrs_before"] = {SQL_COPT_SS_ACCESS_TOKEN: token_struct}

connection_url = URL.create(
        "mssql+pyodbc",
        host="tcp:<resource_name>.sql.azuresynapse.net,1433",
        database="<database>",
        query={
            "driver": "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server",
            "LongAsMax": "Yes",
            # "autocommit": "True",
            "MARS_Connection": "Yes", # For chunk reads
        },
    )

conn = st.connection(
    "synapse",
    "sql",
    url=connection_url,
    # autocommit=True,
    connect_args=dict(ignore_no_transaction_on_rollback=True),
)

event.listen(target=conn.engine, identifier="do_connect", fn=provide_token)

df = conn.query("SELECT * FROM schema.database;", ttl=timedelta(days=1))
```

As a workaround, how should I set the event listener so it does not break when the object is depickled from cache? Any other suggestion on how to deal with this?

title: Native authentication support for Streamlit
body:
### Summary

We are investigating approaches to add native authentication support for Streamlit, as it is one of the top most requested community features. This is a rough proposal for how it might work, which is shared for your feedback.

### Goals

**Goal 1:** Provide the building blocks for integrating more robust auth solutions including:
- documented support for reading headers (replace the undocumented but heavily used `_get_websocket_headers()`
- native support for reading and writing cookies ( #861 )
- native redirect ( #7123 )
- hooks to add identity information in `st.user`
- _[longer term]_ Support custom http endpoints ( #439 ) - this will be a bigger effort but know we probably need to get there eventually to have a really robust support
- ??? What else ???

**Goal 2:** Provide an out-of-the-box native integration which covers the most common use cases, especially for developers getting started. To that end, we propose **standardizing on OAuth2 & OpenID Connect as the natively supported protocols in Streamlit**.
- This would be an opinionated and minimal implementation, geared towards integrating with standardized OIDC providers.
- Goal would be, with a few lines of config / secrets, you can be set up with `login()` / `logout()` methods and the users verified email, OAuth2 token, and potentially other claims from a JWT readily available through a standard API (likely attributes on `st.user`).
- Ideally, include an easy integration with cookies support so it's trivial to maintain the user auth session across tabs for some time. However, we still need to investigate whether this is feasible or has other major implications.

**Why OpenID Connect (OIDC)?**
- From our perspective, OIDC seems like the most modern, standardized authentication protocol we can use which enables a standard format of user identity claims (including roles / groups) and minimal custom code across providers.
- We also see a wide range of adoption across identity providers both in the consumer space (Google, Apple, etc) and enterprise space (Auth0, AWS Cognito, MSFT Entra ID, etc).
- For most app developers who aren't working in a more sophisticated existing platform, it seems to cover the typical use case for "single sign on" for relatively low fuss and configuration required in the provider side.

**Non-goal: Replace the use of reverse proxy in higher security environments**

We know this practice of running Streamlit behind an auth proxy and forwarding authenticated requests to the app is fairly common among Streamlit usage in bigger companies or those with higher security requirements. We want to build library features that make that easier to run (such as documented headers support) but not replace it or build extremely hardened security into Streamlit, since it isn't our expertise.

But, we think this proposal can still unblock many developers operating in somewhat lower stakes environments who experience a lot of friction today.

### VERY ROUGH API sketch

Here's a very rough first idea of how the API might work for the built-in OIDC.

```toml
# .streamlit/secrets.toml or similar

[auth] # reserved group for defining auth, could also support multiple like [auth.google]
type = "oidc"
provider = "google" # or api_base_url="accounts.google.com"
client_id = "SOME ID"
client_secret = "SOME SECRET"
default_ttl = "7d" # if we have some easy cookie support

```

Once this is configured, you can call some standard methods in the app which will redirect to the appropriate OIDC flow. Streamlit will automatically expose an OAuth2 callback endpoint which handles the response from the identity provider.

In the case below, calling `login()` will simply redirect to the OAuth2 flow. When the user returns from the flow, their identity values will be available in `st.user`. Calling `logout()` will clear the values from `st.user` in that session along with any browser cookies.

```python
# streamlit_app.py

if st.user.logged_in(): # verify log in, including cookie from an earlier session
    st.write(f"Welcome, {st.user.name}!")
    st.sidebar.button("Logout", on_click=st.user.logout)
else:
    st.sidebar.button("Login", on_click=st.user.login)
```

### Other authentication protocols

We know other protocols are used today, such as looking up a username / password in a database (e.g. [Streamlit-Authenticator](https://github.com/mkhorasani/Streamlit-Authenticator)), or more complex delegated authentication schemes like SAML / LDAP. In some cases, the existing plugins / components for these can work pretty well. We'd like to provide some hooks to make them more consistent with the native support (maybe similar to `st.connection`), but it may not be in the initial launch.

### What do you think?

If this proposal and approach sounds good and meets your use case, please give a 👍 . Also, we'd love to hear any comments about what you like, don't like, or would change, or any use case you have which would not be supported. Thanks!!

title: Be able to close cached resources (@st.cache_resource)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`@st.cache_resource` is recommended to use for non-hashable resources like database connections. However, such resources might require closing.

### Why?

`@st.cache_resource` is recommended to use for non-hashable resources like database connection. From the doc:
```
 @st.cache_resource
 def get_database_session(_sessionmaker, url):
     # Create a database connection object that points to the URL.
     return connection
```
However, these resources could require closing (closing the database connection, stopping a `SparkSession`). 

In the current implementation I'm not able to close the connection, requiring the streamlit instance to be restarted. For database connections this will result in dangling connections. 

### How?

Ideally I'd be able to close the resource in the same function similar to [PyTest yields usage](https://docs.pytest.org/en/6.2.x/fixture.html#yield-fixtures-recommended):
```
 @st.cache_resource
 def get_database_session(_sessionmaker, url):
     # Create a database connection object that points to the URL.
     yield connection
     connection.close()
```

Alternatively, perhaps a close callback:
```
 @st.cache_resource(close= lambda con: con.close())
 def get_database_session(_sessionmaker, url):
     # Create a database connection object that points to the URL.
     return connection
```

See:

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.counter = 0

st.rerun()

title: Current recommended way to deal with restarted Streamlit sessions, for both recovering the session state and continuing calculations
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

**Background:**

Unfortunately the platform where we are primarily deploying Streamlit, Palantir Foundry Code Workspaces, randomly restarts Streamlit sessions. It seems they are unable or unwilling to fix this, which is probably the right way to solve the problem, but I am posting here in case others have similar issues, as this could be a more general topic.

If you run a Jupyter notebook in say JupyterLab and then restart the browser, you see in the console that Jupyter reconnects to the session and everything is preserved nicely.

However, we all know that when Streamlit is restarted (and I personally think Streamlit could be utilized as a more user-friendly Jupyter notebook), nothing is preserved.

We have partially combatted the problem by allowing the user to manually save the session state, but if our users forget, then their work since their last save is lost. Note a consideration at least in our case is that we are performing sometimes complex analyses on large datasets, so at times we have 10-15 GB of data in the session state and are running hours-long computations using multiple cores. Each manual save can therefore take a significant amount of time (~a minute).

**Questions:**

1. What is Streamlit's current recommended way to _continuously_ save the session state so that if the session is randomly restarted, all is recovered. This has to be a fast process since again we often have large datasets in memory.
2. What is Streamlit's current recommended way to persist jobs being run by Streamlit instead of them getting killed if the session is restarted?

Thanks so much in advance for your help!

title: Exponential slowdown in Streamlit as the number of widgets increases (starting in v1.34)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

There is an exponential slowdown in Streamlit as the number of input widgets is increases. This started happening with the 1.34 release and is tied to PR #8529. Calling [`get_session_state()`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/number_input.py#L390) in the widgets is triggering this [dict comp method](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py#L370) exponentially more times than previously. For a simple app containing 200 number inputs, there is a 50x increase in calls to `_reverse_key_wid_map` which causes the app to take over 1s to re-load locally (vs ~0.2s with release 1.33). Here is a plot of the number of calls vs the number of inputs:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b0ef9c9-49c4-482b-85d9-9684e41f523d)

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time
import random

NUM_TABS = 10
NUM_INPUTS = 20


def create_inputs(t):
    for i in range(NUM_INPUTS):
        key = f"tab_{t + 1}_input_{i + 1}_value"
        if key in st.session_state:
            value = st.session_state[key]
        else:
            value = random.randint(0, 100000)
        st.number_input(
            label=f"Number Input {i + 1}",
            value=value,
            min_value=0,
            step=1,
            format="%d",
            key=key,
        )


def main():
    st.title("My dummy app")
    with st.container(border=True, height=500):
        tabs = st.tabs([f"Tab {i + 1}" for i in range(NUM_TABS)])
        for t, tab in enumerate(tabs):
            with tab:
                create_inputs(t)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import cProfile
    from pstats import Stats

    pr = cProfile.Profile()
    pr.enable()

    start_time = time.time()
    main()
    st.info(f"run time: {time.time() - start_time:.3f} seconds")

    pr.disable()
    stats = Stats(pr)
    stats.sort_stats("tottime").print_stats(10)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app using Streamlit version 1.33
2. Adjust `NUM_TABS` value from 1 to 10 and monitor the `cProfile` output
3. Switch to Streamlit version 1.34 or above
4. Repeat step 2

here is a screenshot of the cProfile output with Streamlit 1.33 using 200 widgets:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c39e939-5cc9-407a-99f1-e1c9de0257b2)

and here's a screenshot using Streamlit 1.34:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3da40e2d-025c-4752-9a96-6b10b233a0bd)

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Current Behavior

_No response_

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Streamlit version: 1.33 vs 1.34+
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome

title: Using AppTest, st.dialog does not execute code within st.buttons
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In previous versions of `streamlit`, I built a confirmation dialog using [streamlit_modal](https://github.com/teamtv/streamlit_modal), which worked fine - also during testing using `streamlit.testing.AppTest`.

Now I transitioned to the new `@st.dialog` decorator, because it feels smoother and is easier to use. But I discovered some strange behavior during testing:  
The code inside the confirmation button, which is inside the dialog, is never executed during testing.

My current understanding is, that the state of the confirmation button is set to `True`, but during the necessary `at.rerun()` the state of the button to show the dialog is reset - therefore the dialog and the button function are not executed again.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault('confirm', False)

@st.dialog('Confirmation')
def confirmation_dialog():

    if st.button('confirm', key='k_btn_confirm'):
        st.session_state.confirm = True
        st.rerun()

st.write(st.session_state.confirm)

if st.button('Show confirmation dialog', key='k_btn_confirmation_dialog'):
    confirmation_dialog()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Save the code example as `app.py`
2. Start the application using `streamlit run app.py`
3. Observe, that the confirmation dialog works as expected

Now create an additional file `test_dialog.py` with the following content:
```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest


def test_dialog():
    at = AppTest('app.py', default_timeout=30)
    at.run()

    at.button('k_btn_confirmation_dialog').click()
    at.run()

    # at.button('k_btn_confirmation_dialog').click()
    at.button('k_btn_confirm').click()
    at.run()

    assert at.session_state.confirm is True

```

4. Run `pytest` - the final check will fail
5. Include the commented-out line, retriggering the dialog to be shown
6. Re-run `pytest` - the test will now succeed

### Expected Behavior

I would expect `st.dialog` to behave the same way during normal execution and testing.

### Current Behavior

Currently the test fails because the code inside the button `k_btn_confirm` is never executed.

```python
>       assert at.session_state.confirm is True
E       AssertionError: assert False is True

FAILED test_dialog.py::test_dialog - AssertionError: assert False is True
```

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.39.0
- Python version: 3.11.9
- Operating System: Windows 10 Enterprise, Version 22H2, OS build 19045.5011
- Browser: Microsoft Edge for Business, Version 130.0.2849.68 (64-bit)


### Additional Information

My impression is, that this issue is caused by a number of factors playing together:
* `st.rerun()` in button callbacks is a no-op  
requiring you to use the `if st.button(...):` clause
* `AppTest` requires explicit `.run()` calls after widget interaction  
otherwise the fragment would rerun and execute the code within the button
* there is no way to interact with `st.dialog` / `st.fragment` from `AppTest`  
e.g. triggering a rerun of the fragment instead of the whole app

title: Session State convenience function for initialization
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It'd be nice for Session State to have a convenience method for initializing it.

### Why?

Many apps have boilerplate code:
```python
if "my_key" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_key = "default_value"
```
If there are multiple keys, you might shortcut the logical test to check for one and initialize all others:
```python
if "A" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.A = "A"
    st.session_state.B = "B"
    st.session_state.C = "C"
```
If any of the keys were associated to a widget and the widget wasn't continuously rendered, you could have a situation will all keys initialized on session start, but maybe "B" or "C" got deleted later. Thus, to be really thorough, you'd need:

```python
session_init = {"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"}
for key, value in session_init.items():
    st.session_state[key] = value
```

It might be nice to have a convenience function to handle the latter:

```python
st.session_state.from_dict({"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"})
```

A parameter could be used to distinguish between initializing (set if not exists), updating (dictionary merge), or full replacement (delete other keys).


### How?

Similar to how `st.query_params` is a dict-like interface with a few extra functions, `st.session_state` could get a convenience function or two.

title: Buttons inside fragments do not interrupt the "outside" code
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a button inside a fragment is clicked, if the "outside" code is still running, the button does not trigger (neither the callback nor the fragment rerun) until the outside code is finished. I am not sure if this is intentional, but it seems wrong.

```py
import streamlit as st
import time

def callback():
    print("Callback called")
   
@st.fragment
def frag():
    print("Fragment start")
    if st.button("Click me", on_click=callback):
        print("Button clicked")
    print("Fragment end")

frag()

print("Sleep start")
time.sleep(5)
print("Sleep end")
```

When started, if the button is clicked during sleep, the output would be:
```
Fragment start
Fragment end
Sleep start
Sleep end
Callback called
Fragment start
Button clicked
Fragment end
```

Without the `@st.fragment`, output is:
```
Fragment start
Fragment end
Sleep start
Callback called
Fragment start
Button clicked
Fragment end
Sleep start
Sleep end
Sleep end
```

This makes more sense to me, although I am not sure under which circumstances the "previous" process is left to finish (as in this case), vs. being stopped. Is there a way to control this?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: MacOS


### Edit

I found that there is a similar issue too when the code inside the fragment is not yet finished.

title: Preserve session state (e.g. in file, database, or localstorage)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a mechanism to preserve widget state or anything in `st.session_state` across sessions, e.g. by putting it into a local file, or a small database that we run alongside the Streamlit app, or an external database, or localstorage. 

### Why?

The most common use case here is being able to close the tab, come back to it later, and pick up where you left off. Also somewhat related is preserving session state across multiple pages of a multipage app (see #5813), even though I think we should find a better solution for this. 

### How?

I think we should look at whether we can find a solution that relates to syncing widget state to query params (see #302) since they basically do the same thing, just storing the values in different places. Maybe something like a parameter on every widget `sync="query_params"|"database"|"localstorage"|...`.

It would also be great to make this extensible, so that experienced devs can configure their own places where the session state should be stored (e.g. an external database).

title: Concurrency issues with `st.data_editor` `on_change` callback: Using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` leads to multiple processing or potential data loss
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

**Issue Description:**

When a user edits cells in the `st.data_editor` object, the `on_change` callback function is triggered. If the user makes additional edits while the `on_change` callback is still running, some edits are processed multiple times (in this case, twice for edits of the first interaction and once for the second interaction) when using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` to process the user edits. This occurs because the callback is threaded, and the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` object still includes the edits from the previous user interaction.

**Additional Issue:**

Attempting to fix this revealed another issue: If the `on_change` callback for a previous call takes longer to execute than the latest call, the Streamlit page reloads before the previous `on_change` callbacks are finished. As a result, not all cells of the `st.data_editor` object are updated, leading to potential loss of user edits. This seems to be fixed by using `threading.Lock()` in the on_change callback function.

**Request:**
I found a solution to this, but would like to know if I just use the `st.data_editor` object and corresponding `on_change` callback in a way that they were not meant to be used (passing/using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` in the callback).
-> Is there another method to handle user edits on a dataframe, which ensures that those edits are processed exactly once, so neither multiple times nor never before the Streamlit page or `st.fragment` get reloaded?

### Why?

This is relevant when streaming user edits to a backend database, as potentially user edits are send multiple times to the backend, which causes unnecessary traffic, or edits are lost and not sent to the backend at all.

### How?

Solution (including filtering of the `st.data_editor`'s session state and locking threads during the `on_change` callback):
```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import threading
import time

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

# Initialize session state variables if not already done
if "applied_edits" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["applied_edits"] = {}
if "df" not in st.session_state:
    data = np.zeros((1000, 30))
    columns = [f"Column {i + 1}" for i in range(30)]
    df_init = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=columns)
    totals_row = pd.DataFrame(df_init.sum(axis=0)).T
    st.session_state.df = pd.concat([totals_row, df_init], ignore_index=True)
    st.session_state.df["Totals"] = st.session_state.df.sum(axis=1)
if "call" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["call"] = 0
if "lock" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["lock"] = threading.Lock()


def df_on_change(df):
    with st.session_state["lock"]:
        print(f"on_change call: {st.session_state['call']}")
        # Get a copy of all edited rows in this session
        all_edits = st.session_state["df_editor"]["edited_rows"]
        # Filter out the new edits/changes that were/are not processed in a previous call of the df_on_change function
        edited_rows = {
            row: {
                col: val
                for col, val in changes.items()
                if (row not in st.session_state["applied_edits"])
                or (st.session_state["applied_edits"][row].get(col) != val)
            }
            for row, changes in all_edits.items()
        }
        # Update the record of applied edits so the filter above can be applied in the next call of the df_on_change function once again
        for row, changes in edited_rows.items():
            if not changes:
                continue  # no new changes for this row
            if row not in st.session_state["applied_edits"]:
                st.session_state["applied_edits"][row] = {}
            for col, val in changes.items():
                st.session_state["applied_edits"][row][col] = val

        # Log the filtered edits for debugging
        print(f"session state of data editor: {st.session_state['df_editor']}")
        print(f"New edits to apply: {edited_rows}")
        print(f"Applied edits history: {st.session_state['applied_edits']}")

        # Apply the new changes to the DataFrame
        for row, changes in edited_rows.items():
            for col, val in changes.items():
                print(f"writing value {val} to row {row} and column {col}")
                df.loc[row, col] = val
                # simulate a on_change function that requires a long execution time
                time.sleep(1)

        # Recompute totals row based on all data below it
        df.loc[0] = df.iloc[1:].sum(axis=0)
        df["Totals"] = df.sum(axis=1)

        st.toast("Data updated successfully!")
        st.session_state["call"] += 1


# Use st.data_editor with the on_change callback
st.data_editor(
    st.session_state.df,
    use_container_width=True,
    num_rows="fixed",
    disabled=["Totals"],  # prevent editing the totals row
    column_order=[f"Column {i + 1}" for i in range(30)] + ["Totals"],
    key="df_editor",
    on_change=df_on_change,
    args=[st.session_state.df],
    row_height=20,
)
```

In the demo videos below, the user first adds 9 cells at once and then does single cell changes afterwards (on other cells).

Demo video of the code above (terminal output also shows that each edit/cell is just processed once, which is not the case when not filtering the `st.data_editor`'s session state):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e924ae7-4cc0-4c96-8029-97c98f872548

Demo video without thread locking:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aac91a5d-536c-4a44-97c0-1219d80684af

title: Create an interface to manage frontend state
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

We have `st.session_state` which allows us to manage widget values. I'm proposing an interface to work with frontend states.


### Why?

We recently introduced a pattern for setting the placeholder text of `st.chat_input`. We used `st.session_state` to do this, but the pattern is very different of other uses because `st.chat_input` is more like a trigger than a stateful widget.

It seems more scalable to have a separate interface for "setting stuff on the frontend but not implicitly sending the information back to the Python server or triggering a rerun."

### How?

`st.frontend_state` would have similar access as `st.session_state`: for example,
* `st.frontend_state.<element_key>.focus()` would be a command to set focus on the frontend.
* `st.frontend_state.<element_key>.state("collapsed")` or `state("expanded")` could be available for the sidebar or expanders. (We set the initial state from the backend, but users are free to expand or collapse these items from the frontend without triggering a rerun.)
* `st.frontend_state.<element_state>.disabled(True)` or `disabled(False)` could be used to disable widgets at the beginning of a run and re-enable them at the end of a run if you want to prevent script run interruptions. (As an auto-protection, any widget that is enabled within the widget command but disabled through frontend state must automatically be re-enabled at the end of a script run if the developer didn't do so themselves.)

The idea of `st.frontend_state` would be to cause state changes that don't themselves cause reruns or otherwise report to the Python backend. (Edgecase: If a use has focus on a widget and a partial edit, then forcing focus elsewhere should technically cause a rerun and submit that partial edit, so app developers would be responsible for using focus appropriately.)

### Additional Context

`st.frontend_state` takes inspiration from both `st.session_state` and `AppTest`. It could be used for two-way communication, but be much less restrictive than Session State. That is, there'd be no problem calling it multiple times. You could "retrieve" the current frontend state multiple times if you wanted to detect if the user had expanded/collapsed something in the middle of a rerun. Unlike states that immediately trigger a rerun and are more rigidly controlled within a script run, the "frontend only" states can be set and retrieved multiple times during a run, in general.

Another example: suppose `st.tabs` gets an `on_change` parameter. `on_change="ignore"` is the default and it operates as it does currently, with the tab selection being a frontend state. If we set `on_change="rerun"` or assign a callable, it becomes a widget. In the first case, you could access or set the current tab through `st.frontend_state` (and not impact the flow of the rerun). In the latter case, the selection is a "value" that must be controlled through `st.session_state`, not `st.frontend_state`.

title: Add support for dynamic tab badges or persistent tab keys
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

**Description:**  
Currently, Streamlit's `st.tabs()` does not support dynamically updating tab titles without resetting the selected tab. In applications where the tab title needs to reflect real-time counts (e.g., number of items, unread notifications, or messages), updating the title causes the tabs to re-render completely, and the first tab becomes selected by default.  

This makes it difficult to provide live feedback to users without disrupting their current view. A few potential solutions could be:  

1. **Built-in badge support:** Allow tabs to display a small badge (count or indicator) alongside the title, which can be updated dynamically without affecting the selected tab.  
2. **Persistent tab keys:** Allow developers to assign unique keys to tabs so that updating the title does not reset the selected tab.  
3. **Dynamic title updates without re-rendering:** Provide a mechanism for updating the displayed title independently of the tab component's internal state.  

**Example use case:**

```python
import streamlit as st

tab_titles = ["First", "Second", "Third"]
for i, title in enumerate(tab_titles):
    key = f"counter_{i}"
    if key not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state[key] = 0

dynamic_titles = [f"{title} (+{st.session_state[f'counter_{i}']})" 
                  for i, title in enumerate(tab_titles)]

tabs = st.tabs(dynamic_titles)  # Updating dynamic_titles resets selected tab

for i, tab in enumerate(tabs):
    with tab:
        st.write(f"### {tab_titles[i]}")
        if st.button("Increment counter", key=f"btn_{i}"):
            st.session_state[f"counter_{i}"] += 1
            st.rerun()
```

Currently, updating the `dynamic_titles` list causes the tabs to re-render and always select the first tab, which is not ideal for UX. Adding badge support or persistent tab keys would solve this problem elegantly.


### Why?

_No response_

### How?

For example:

```python
home, analytics, settings = st.tabs([
    st.Tab(title="Home", icon="🏠", badge=32),
    st.Tab(title="Analytics", icon="📊", badge=5),
    st.Tab(title="Settings", icon="⚙️")
])
```

Or just give option for key to stay persistent:
```python
home, analytics, settings = st.tabs(["Home", "Analytics", "Settings"], key="persistent_tabs")
```

title: Easier cross-filtering between charts/dataframes
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

In BI dashboards, you often want to cross-filter between charts and/or dataframes. Building this in Streamlit via chart/dataframe selections isn't very straightforward. Could we find an easier solution?

### Why?

Two example use cases to illustrate the problem:

- Simple example: You have one chart and one dataframe. If you select some rows in the dataframe, the chart updates to show only those data points. If you select some data points in the chart, the dataframe updates to show only the corresponding rows. 
- Complex example: A dashboard with multiple charts. If you click on any chart, all the other charts update to only the data that was selected in the first chart. Ideally, this should also support then selecting data in a 2nd or 3rd chart to further drill down. 

It's possible to build this in Streamlit with chart/dataframe selections, but not very straightforward since:

1. You need to parse the selection and then manually filter the data in other visualizations based on what was selected. 
2. It's not easy to update a visualization that is "above" the one where data was selected, due to Streamlit's rerun model. You'd need to save all selections centrally in `st.session_state` and then update charts from there. 
3. The entire page will rerun on every selection, making this potentially slow. 

### How?

Probably needs a good amount of thinking but some rough ideas:

1. Allow passing the key of another element to `on_select`. This would then automatically sync that element whenever some data is selected in the current one. Or maybe it should even sync in both ways?

  ```python
  st.line_chart(..., key="chart1")
  st.dataframe(..., on_select="chart1")
  ```

2. Adding a command like `st.cross_filter` to cross filter between multiple charts/dataframes.

  ```python
  st.line_chart(..., key="chart1")
  st.plotly_chart(..., key="chart2")
  st.dataframe(..., key="dataframe")
  st.cross_filter("chart1", "chart2", "dataframe")
  ```

One big problem here is probably making sure all visualizations have access to the same data/can filter. E.g. if I have a pie chart showing the gender of all people, how can we make sure clicking on "Female" lets the other charts know how to filter their own data?

### Additional Context

title: Memory leak caused by session state persisting after tab closed
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

It looks like streamlit is never cleaning the session state after the tab is closed. Due to this, we're seeing memory usage increase overtime.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np

def format_memory(mb):
    """Format memory in MB to human readable format"""
    if mb > 1024:
        return f"{mb/1024:.2f} GB"
    return f"{mb:.2f} MB"

st.title("Streamlit Memory Management Test")
st.write("This app tests how Streamlit handles large objects in session state")

# Initialize session state
if 'memory_objects' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.memory_objects = {}

if 'allocation_count' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.allocation_count = 0

# Controls
col1, col2, col3 = st.columns(3)

with col1:
    size_mb = st.slider("Object Size (MB)", 1, 500, 50)
    
with col2:
    if st.button("Allocate Memory"):
        # Create a large numpy array
        array_size = int((size_mb * 1024 * 1024) / 8)  # 8 bytes per float64
        large_array = np.random.random(array_size)
        
        # Store in session state
        key = f"object_{st.session_state.allocation_count}"
        st.session_state.memory_objects[key] = large_array
        st.session_state.allocation_count += 1
        
        st.success(f"Allocated {format_memory(size_mb)} object: {key}")
        st.rerun()

with col3:
    if st.button("Clear All Memory"):
        st.session_state.memory_objects.clear()
        st.session_state.allocation_count = 0
        st.success("Cleared all allocated objects")
        st.rerun()

# Display allocated objects
if st.session_state.memory_objects:
    st.subheader("Allocated Objects")
    
    total_size = 0
    for key, obj in st.session_state.memory_objects.items():
        obj_size = obj.nbytes / 1024 / 1024  # Convert to MB
        total_size += obj_size
        
        col1, col2, col3 = st.columns([2, 2, 1])
        with col1:
            st.write(f"**{key}**")
        with col2:
            st.write(f"{format_memory(obj_size)}")
        with col3:
            if st.button("Delete", key=f"del_{key}"):
                del st.session_state.memory_objects[key]
                st.rerun()
    
    st.metric("Total Allocated", format_memory(total_size))
else:
    st.info("No objects allocated yet")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run this code example with `streamlit run memory_test_app.py --server.disconnectedSessionTTL=1`
2. Use the "Allocate Memory" button to create some objects.
3. Confirm (on mac os Activity Monitor) that memory usage matches "Total Allocated".
4. Delete an "Allocated Object" using the button.

6. Close the tab and wait.

### Summary

I encounter an issue when using streamlit with the CLI option `--server.runOnSave true`, where my code is rerun multiple times when I modify it. However, if I don't use this option and I activate the `Always rerun` from the web interface, my code is rerun only once on modifications.

This issue happens after `streamlit>=1.47`

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

print("run")
st.write("run")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Make sure you have `streamlit>=1.47` installed 
2. Run the above script using `streamlit run  --server.runOnSave true tmp.py`
3. The console should display a single `run` line
4. Modify and save the `tmp.py` file, by adding an empty line at the end for instance
5. Now, the `run` line shoudl be displayed multiple times

### Expected Behavior

The `run` line should be displayed once for every modification of the `tmp.py` file.

### Current Behavior

The `run` line is displayed multiple times for every modification of the `tmp.py` file

### Is this a regression?

- Python version: 3.10.18
- Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04
- Browser: Firefox and Edge


### Additional Information

If I run the script  `streamlit run tmp.py` and I activate the `Always rerun` from the web interface, the `run` line is displayed only once for every modification of `tmp.py`
Also, if I install `streamlit<1.47`, I have the expected behavior even if using the CLI option.

title: Multiselect default values not respected in @st.fragment with on_change and session state logic (regression in 1.50.0)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In Streamlit 1.50.0, I encountered a bug where st.multiselect would ignore default values that were correctly initialized in st.session_state. This happened inside a @st.fragment, when using both on_change callbacks and session state re-initialization after a parent widget change.

The exact same logic worked perfectly in 1.49.1.
Unfortunately, I couldn’t reproduce the issue in a minimal code snippet — so it seems related to a more complex interaction between fragments, nested state logic, and conditional UI loading.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
None — minimal examples failed to reproduce, though the symptoms consistently occur in a real app.

However, I attempted many combinations similar to the one below — all of which worked fine:

import streamlit as st

@st.fragment
def example():
    patient = st.selectbox("Patient", ["", "A", "B"], key="pat", on_change=lambda: st.session_state.pop("sel", None))
    options = ["Conv1", "Conv2"]
    if "sel" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state["sel"] = ["Conv1"]
    st.write("Session default:", st.session_state["sel"])
    selected = st.multiselect("Conversations", options=options, default=st.session_state["sel"], key="multi", on_change=lambda: None)
    st.write("Selected:", selected)

example()


----

Real code snippet:

...
_key = "conversation_multiselect"
    # Selected conversations
    if len(conversation_ids) == 1:
        disabled = True
        # Unused variable, just a holder
        _ = st.multiselect(label="Select **conversations**",
                           options=conversation_ids,
                           disabled=disabled,
                           default=_saved_conversations,
                           key=f"{_key}_disabled")

        st.warning("No conversations found. Please select/add a conversation first.")
        _related_conversations = []

    else:
        if "selected_conversation" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state.selected_conversation = _saved_conversations

        # due to streamlit 1.50.0 this line is needed, otherwise default selection is no loading. 
        st.session_state[_key] = st.session_state.selected_conversation

        _related_conversations = st.multiselect(label="Select **conversations**",
                                                options=conversation_ids,
                                                default=st.session_state.selected_conversation,
                                                on_change=on_conversation_change,
                                                key=_key,
                                                help="Select conversations related to the patient. These will be saved as related documents.",
                                                )

...
```

### Steps To Reproduce

I was not able to reproduce with a minimal example, but try this: 

In the full app:

1. Change a parent selector (e.g., patient)
2. Session state is updated or re-initialized
3. A multiselect inside a fragment tries to use the updated default from session state
4. It shows empty, even though st.session_state[...] has the correct value

### Expected Behavior

When a widget’s default= is populated from st.session_state[...], it should display the default value, even when wrapped in a fragment and triggered after on_change.

### Current Behavior

After on_change resets a session state key (e.g., deleting st.session_state["selected_conversation"]), and the widget is rerendered inside a fragment, the default= is silently ignored — despite the session state being correctly updated before rendering.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.50.0 (works in 1.49.1)
- Python version:3.12.9
- Operating System: Win 11 / WSL2 Ubuntu, ALmaLinux9
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

Strange issue and sorry that I was not able to reproduce with a minimal code. But this line solves the problem: 

st.session_state[_key] = st.session_state.selected_conversation

I'm am happy to help.

title: Support real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, Streamlit requires rerunning the entire script to refresh visual elements such as charts or plots.
This feature request suggests adding native support for incremental or real-time updates to chart components, allowing smoother dashboards for live data without script reruns.

### Why?

I often build dashboards with data that changes every few seconds (e.g. IoT sensors, live logs, financial data).
The current rerun mechanism makes the app flicker and consume excessive CPU, as every update forces Streamlit to re-execute all widgets and scripts.
A lighter update mechanism would make Streamlit much more efficient for real-time applications.

### How?

Introduce a new method, for example:

chart = st.line_chart(initial_data)
chart.update(new_data)


or a context manager such as:

with st.chart("my_chart") as chart:
    chart.update(data)


This would allow partial UI updates for selected components instead of full script reruns, leading to faster refresh rates and better performance.

### Additional Context

This feature would be highly valuable for real-time dashboards and data streaming use cases.
Similar functionality exists in libraries like Plotly Dash (dcc.Interval) or Bokeh Server.
Discussion inspiration: Streamlit Community Forum – Real-time dashboard performance

body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary When setting the value of a `st.selectbox` via the session state API (to something else than the first option) and interacting with the selectbox (opening it and closing it without selecting an option), the selectbox visually switches to the first option (even though the backend keeps returning the value originally set via the session state API). ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st with st.container(horizontal=True): for value in (1, 2, 3): if st.button(f"Set {value}"): st.session_state["key"] = value selected_option = st.selectbox("Select", options=(1, 2, 3), index=0, key="key") st.text(f"Selected option: {selected_option}") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Try the above code example. 2. Click on `Set 2`. 3. Click on the selectbox. 4. Click outside the selectbox. ### Expected Behavior The selectbox should keep displaying `2`. ### Current Behavior The selectbox displays `1` (the first option). Additionally, the text below still displays `Selected option: 2`, exacerbating the discrepancy between the frontend and the backend. This is the value returned by `st.selectbox` or the `st.session_state["key"]`. You can reproduce it again if you click on `Set 3`, click on the selectbox, and click outside the selectbox. Once you select an option in the selectbox, the bug won't happen for the duration of the session. Refresh the page (new session) to reproduce the bug again. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.52.2 - Python version: 3.11.9 - Operating System: MacOS - Browser: Chrome ### Additional Information This bug does NOT occur if the `index` argument is provided to `st.selectbox`, but... If I set `index=None`, the selectbox becomes clearable, and I don't want that in my use case. ```python if "key" not in st.session_state: st.session_state["key"] = 2 selected_option = st.selectbox("Select", options=(1, 2, 3), index=None, key="key") st.text(f"Selected option: {selected_option}") ``` If I set `index=1` (or any other integer greater than 0), the selectbox behaves perfectly, but it shows the following warning. ```python if "key" not in st.session_state: st.session_state["key"] = 2 selected_option = st.selectbox("Select", options=(1, 2, 3), index=1, key="key") st.text(f"Selected option: {selected_option}") ```
