A custom component that binds those keys cannot keep them: even a capture-phase listener calling `preventDefault()`, `stopPropagation()` and `stopImmediatePropagation()` sees the key and the app still acts on it. This makes single-letter keyboard interfaces — the norm in accessible visualization libraries, where a blind user drives a chart from the keyboard — impossible to build on Streamlit's non-iframe component path. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python # app.py import streamlit as st st.session_state["runs"] = st.session_state.get("runs", 0) + 1 st.write(f"RUNS={st.session_state['runs']}") st.text_input("a text input") st.button("a button") st.markdown( '
' "a custom widget
", unsafe_allow_html=True, ) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Save the snippet above as `app.py` and run `streamlit run app.py`. 2. Click the bordered div to focus it, press r, and watch `RUNS` increment. 3. To confirm a component cannot defend the key, run this in the browser console and press r again with the div focused: ```js document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'r') { e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation(); } }, true); // capture phase — the earliest a listener can run ``` ### Expected Behavior A component should be able to opt out of app-level key handling for the region it owns, or the exemption should extend to focus inside a registered custom component. ### Current Behavior The capture-phase listener above receives the event, and the app reruns anyway. Measured on **Streamlit 1.61.1**, driving a real browser and checking whether the app acted: | focused element | `r` | `c` | |---|---|---| | page body | app acts | app acts | | `
` | **app acts** | **app acts** | | `

title: Allow interactive resizing of `st.columns` via drag-and-drop
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `resizable: bool = False` parameter to `st.columns` that lets users resize columns by dragging the border between them. When enabled, a border indicator appears on hover between adjacent columns, and dragging adjusts their widths interactively. Resizing is purely client-side and does not trigger a rerun. Specced in [PR #14687](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14687).

### Why?

Column widths in `st.columns` are static today — once set via `spec`, they can't be adjusted without changing code and rerunning. Interactive resizing helps with dashboard customization, data exploration (temporarily expand a column to see more), fine-tuning responsive layouts, and adjusting proportions live during demos/presentations. Current workarounds (layout presets via `st.selectbox`, CSS hacks in custom components, or just accepting fixed layouts) are clunky or fragile.

Related: #5003 (deactivate responsiveness of `st.columns`), #6592 (configurable column responsiveness threshold).

### How?

```python
st.columns(
    spec,
    *,
    gap="small",
    vertical_alignment="top",
    border=False,
    width="stretch",
    resizable=False,  # NEW
)
```

- `resizable=False` (default): current fixed-width behavior, no handles.
- `resizable=True`: drag the border between adjacent columns to resize.

Behavior (from the spec):
- **Hover indicator** + `col-resize` cursor over the resize area; border fades in/out (150ms).
- **Drag** resizes only the two adjacent columns; total row width is preserved (neighbor shrinks as one grows); other columns unchanged.
- **Double-click** the handle resets the adjacent pair to their original `spec` proportions.
- **Minimum width** of 64px prevents collapse; throttled updates for performance.
- **Keyboard**: Arrow Left/Right resize in 10px increments when focused.
- **Accessibility**: handles use `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `aria-valuenow/min/max`, and visible focus indicators (WCAG 2.1).
- **Touch**: drag works via touch; indicator shows on touch start.
- **Narrow viewports**: when columns stack (below `theme.breakpoints.columns`, 640px), handles are hidden and reappear when it widens.
- **State**: resized widths persist within the session (React state) and reset on refresh, a `spec`/column-count change, or stack/unstack.

### Alternatives considered (from the spec)

- `resizable: bool` (preferred) vs `resize_mode: Literal["off", "drag"]` — boolean chosen to match the existing `border=True` precedent and the binary nature of the feature; can migrate to an enum later if multiple resize modes are demanded.
- Naming: `resizable` over `adjustable` (too generic) / `flexible` (clashes with flexbox).

### Out of scope (future work)

Persist widths across sessions, snap-to-grid, per-column `min_width`/`max_width`, `on_resize` callback, and named/saveable layout presets.

### Additional Context

- Spec: [PR #14687 — \`[spec] Allow interactive resizing of st.columns\`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14687) (`specs/2026-04-08-resizable-columns/product-spec.md`).

title: Minimize `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` errors
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Reduce how often developers hit `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` (duplicate widget/element ID) errors by making element ID generation smarter about the surrounding container context — so that identical widgets placed in different containers (chat messages, fragments, columns, etc.) don't collide without the developer having to manually craft unique `key`s everywhere.

### Why?

It's increasingly common to have repeating identical widgets across different chat messages, fragment calls, or columns. Today the developer must manage and track a unique `key` for each, which adds a lot of boilerplate and complexity. This is especially painful in chat/LLM apps (in-chat interactive widgets, code-eval "run" buttons, generated suggestion buttons) — and for LLM-generated code it can be nearly impossible to solve, since the model may emit duplicate widgets across messages. `st.form` already avoids this within forms (the `form_id` is part of the ID), which shows the approach can work more broadly.

This is a high-impact papercut: `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` is the **No. 3 most thrown uncaught exception type**, occurring in ~**0.5% of all apps**.

A related pain point: some elements raise `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` and tell you to add a `key`, but **don't actually support a `key` argument**, leaving no clean fix. Examples:
- #11424 — showing the same `st.plotly_chart` multiple times raises `StreamlitDuplicateElementId`.
- #11360 — multiple `st.audio` calls with the same parameters and `autoplay=True` raise a duplicate error that prompts you to add a key, but `st.audio` has no `key`.

### How?

Incorporate more of the container context into an element's ID computation, focusing on **stable, explicit signals** (not user-facing text). Ideas:

- **Wrapping container keys:** automatically include the `key` of wrapping containers / `st.fragment` / `st.form` (those that support keys) in the child element's ID computation. Only for containers that have an explicit key set.
  - If we do this, it strengthens the case for **adding `key` to more containers and elements** — see #9580 and the concrete cases #11424 (`st.plotly_chart`) and #11360 (`st.audio`), plus #6152.
- **Re-evaluate key namespaces and parent-key reuse:** regular element keys, form IDs, and fragment definition keys are currently tracked in separate registries. `st.form` already contributes its `form_id` to the auto-generated IDs of unkeyed children; fragment keys identify fragment definitions but are not currently part of regular child element ID computation. Consider both:
  - Reusing explicit form / fragment / keyed-container keys as stable parent context for **unkeyed** descendants.
  - Whether form and fragment keys should participate in the same duplicate-key checks as regular element keys, or remain separate namespaces that only contribute parent context.

  Treat registry unification as a compatibility decision: the same string can currently be reused between some form / fragment and regular-element keys, and one keyed fragment definition can intentionally run from multiple call sites. Preserve the rule that an explicit child `key` is authoritative and independent of its container.
- **Column index in `st.columns`:** include the column number in the ID computation so the same widget in different columns of the same `st.columns` call doesn't collide.
- **Parent container types:** include the parent container type(s) as part of the ID computation.

**Important caution — be conservative about what goes into ID generation.** Adding container context to the ID changes element identity, which has a subtle downside: a widget that **dynamically moves between containers** (e.g. its wrapping container changes across reruns) would get a new ID and thus lose its identity and state. This is the main risk to weigh (more so than existing widget state resetting on upgrade), and it can be fixed by explicitly setting a `key` on that element so its identity no longer depends on the container context. In particular:
- **Do not** include user-facing **labels/titles** of wrapping containers (e.g. expander label, dialog title, popover label, tab name) in the ID — these change often and would be fragile/surprising. Prefer **explicitly set keys** for disambiguation instead.
- Auto-added context must apply **only to widgets without an explicit `key`**. When a user sets an explicit `key="x"`, the ID must **not** include the added container context — an explicit key should always behave predictably and stay stable regardless of the surrounding containers. Think through backwards compatibility / migration carefully.

### Additional Context

- Add `key` to more elements/containers: #9580, and concrete duplicate-ID cases where no `key` is available today: #11424 (`st.plotly_chart`), #11360 (`st.audio`).
- Related: #6152 (composable/reusable component API for larger apps).
- `st.form` already includes `form_id` in widget ID generation — a useful precedent.
- There is an older internal product spec exploring options (implicit container key-prefix, adding `key`/`key_prefix` to containers, best-practice docs, or fixing duplicate IDs via enumeration). This issue intentionally leans toward the conservative, explicit-key-based approaches from that discussion.

title: Deprecate widget callback `args`/`kwargs` in favor of `functools.partial`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Deprecate the `args` and `kwargs` parameters that widgets currently expose for passing arguments to `on_change` / `on_click` callbacks, and recommend `functools.partial` instead. As part of this, support automatically receiving relevant state (e.g. the widget's new value) in the callback, as requested in #5305.

### Why?

- **Redundant API surface:** `args`/`kwargs` exist on essentially every widget purely to forward arguments to callbacks. Python already has a standard, well-understood tool for this — `functools.partial` — so `args`/`kwargs` are extra parameters to learn, document, and maintain on every widget for something the language handles natively.
- **Consistency & simplicity:** removing them shrinks the signature of every widget and aligns with "prefer Pythonic idioms" and "extend/compose over inventing".
- **Better ergonomics for callbacks:** today callbacks often have to read `st.session_state` to find out what value changed, which makes generic reusable handlers awkward. Passing the value (and possibly key) to the callback automatically (#5305) removes that friction.

### How?

- **Recommend `functools.partial`** as the replacement for `args`/`kwargs`:

```python
from functools import partial

def update(param_name, *, value):
    ...

st.selectbox("Pick", options, on_change=partial(update, "selection_1"))
```

- **Deprecate `args`/`kwargs`** on widgets with a long, clearly-communicated deprecation window and docs/migration guidance (they keep working during the deprecation period). See API principle "Graceful Evolution" (3+ months notice, clear migration path).
- **Auto-pass state to callbacks** (#5305): make the widget's new value available to the callback automatically (e.g. as a keyword argument), so reusable/generic handlers don't need to reach into `st.session_state`. The exact mechanism needs design (opt-in signature detection vs. a fixed kwarg) to stay backwards compatible.

### Additional Context

- Incorporates #5305 (pass state as a parameter to the `on_change` callback).
- This is a cross-cutting change affecting all widgets with callbacks (`on_change`/`on_click`), so it warrants a spec and careful, gradual deprecation.

title: Add a developer debug pane for inspecting state, cache, memory, and profiling
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a built-in developer "debug pane" — a panel (e.g. a collapsible sidebar/overlay) that surfaces debug information and dev tools without cluttering the main app. It would visualize `st.session_state` and cache contents, show memory usage and profiling/performance info, and provide a place to dump debug output (`st.help`, variables, etc.). By default it would be visible only to the app developer (not viewers), so developers don't have to comment debug code in and out.

### Why?

Debugging Streamlit apps today means peppering the main UI with `st.write(st.session_state)`, `st.help(...)`, timing prints, etc., then remembering to remove them. There's no first-class way to inspect what's actually going on — state, cache, memory, timings — in a dedicated, developer-only surface. A debug pane (à la [Django Debug Toolbar](https://github.com/jazzband/django-debug-toolbar)) would make development and troubleshooting dramatically easier and keep debug output out of the real app for end users.

### How?

A developer-only container/panel that is disabled by default for viewers other than the app developer. Over time it could host focused tools, for example:

- **State inspector:** visualize `st.session_state` contents.
- **Cache inspector:** visualize `st.cache_data` / `st.cache_resource` contents (and allow clearing).
- **Memory profiling:** memory usage, and how it changes run-over-run.
- **Execution/performance profiling:** time between/within widget calls and functions; distribution of run times run-over-run (e.g. via a profiler like yappi + a viewer like snakeviz).
- **Debug output container:** a scratch area to write `st.help`, dump variables, etc., that doesn't appear in the main window.
- **Variable inspector:** e.g. a selectbox + `st.help`.
- **Element/DOM inspector:** which widgets were rendered, and their inputs/values; last forward/back message (or equivalent).
- **Console logs** and **error context**.
- Possibly a **Python console** at the end of the app to run quick calculations/inspections (like a Jupyter interactive debugger).

Considerations:
- Developer-only visibility by default (not shown to app viewers); tie into a development vs. production mode.
- Start minimal (state + cache inspection) and grow over time.

### Additional Context

- Prior art: [Django Debug Toolbar](https://github.com/jazzband/django-debug-toolbar), [streamlit-forum](https://github.com/snehankekre/streamlit-forum).
- Closely related: #16306 (dedicated development and production modes) — this debug pane is a natural home for the "development mode" dev tools described there.

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
body:
### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

### Expected Behavior

Every value the mounted component sends is readable on the following script run. The explicit `key` makes the element id stable, so a changing `data` payload should not affect delivery.

### Current Behavior

About 25% of values are never delivered. Verified as lost rather than late by scanning the full backend log after all clicks — 0 arrived in a later run.

The element id was logged each run and confirmed identical throughout (`$$ID-b4c118c7288cf7d656c205e58a384db6-stable_key`), so this is not the identity churn that affects unkeyed components.

Three controls on the same harness came out clean. They do not isolate the bug to trigger-on-mount — see Additional Information — but they do narrow which write path is affected:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `setStateValue` on mount, same conditions | 21/21 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, stable `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, churning `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| **`setTriggerValue` on mount, churning `data`** | **5 of 21 lost** |

### Additional Information

**Mechanism.** `setTriggerValue` writes to a synthetic aggregator widget id (`makeTriggerAggregatorId` → `$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<componentId>__events`) and the flush is deferred to a `setTimeout(…, 0)` macrotask. `App.removeInactiveWidgetState()` runs from the `ScriptFinished` → `clearStaleNodes` setState callback and deletes every widget state whose id is not an active *element* id — the aggregator id never is, because it isn't part of the element tree. When that lands before the flush, the trigger is deleted but the rerun is still sent (`sendUpdateWidgetsMessage` uses unfiltered `createWidgetStatesMsg()`), so the script reruns with no trigger.

Mount-time triggers are the most exposed path: the component's `default function` runs behind `await loadAndRunModule(...)` (dynamic `import()` of a blob URL), so it executes a macrotask or more after the commit that mounted it. This also explains the control table — `setStateValue` is immune because it writes the component's real element id, and the event-handler controls passed because letting the app settle means `removeInactive` has already run.

**The `_pending_resets` theory is ruled out.** It is only populated by `mark_page_switch_drops`, which runs on page transitions and skips widgets whose recorded page is the current page, so a single-page app never populates it. (For the record, the original hypothesis was that `_pending_resets` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py` discarded a frontend-resent value on re-registration, which would have made this by design.)

**Related blind spot.** The same synthetic id is invisible to other active-id filters, not just this one: `App.tsx` `onPageChange` sends `getActiveWidgetStates(activeWidgetIds)`, which would likewise drop a pending aggregator. Reaching it would require a trigger and a page navigation in the same macrotask, and dropping a trigger while navigating away is defensible, so no change is planned there. Recorded as an observation only.

**Scope of what was tested.** Measured against this repro on one machine, 235 trials total. It establishes this race as the cause of the loss seen here; it does not rule out other trigger-loss paths. The same race also appears to explain the recurring `bidi_components/basics_test.py::test_trigger_interactions` CI flake — the failure signature (counts unchanged plus `Result` reset to `None`) is what a trigger-less rerun produces — but that link is inferred from the signature, not directly observed. Two prior automated PRs (#14542, #14843) misattributed that flake to a slow iframe round-trip and raised timeouts.

**Open question for Components V2** (replacing the original question here, which is now answered — the drop is a race, not intentional): should `setTriggerValue` during mount be a supported pattern at all? Fixing the race makes it reliable, but it fires on every remount, so churning `data` produces one trigger per remount. That is a semantics decision independent of this bug, and it determines whether this issue closes as fixed or splits into a fix plus a documentation/warning change.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (released wheel, production frontend build)
- Python version: 3.11 · macOS · Chromium
- The ~25% figure is one 21-trial sample on a single machine; treat it as "roughly a quarter" rather than a precise rate.

title: Support caching event-loop-bound async resources across reruns
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched the existing issues for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary.

### Summary

Explore supporting reusable event-loop-bound resources, such as async database connections and HTTP or LLM clients, with `st.cache_resource`.

Async cache support in #16168 awaits a coroutine function and caches its completed return value. This works for loop-independent values such as dataframes, API responses, and configuration.

It does not make a cached resource's event loop persistent. A client created on one short-lived loop—for example, through `asyncio.run()`—may fail when reused from another loop on a later rerun:

```python
@st.cache_resource
async def get_client():
    return SomeAsyncClient()
```

Async `validate` and `on_release` callbacks are also unsupported today. Supporting them is part of the same lifecycle problem tracked by this issue: Streamlit must await validation before deciding whether to serve a cache entry and run cleanup on the resource's owning event loop during eviction, clearing, background replacement, or session shutdown.

### Why isn't this currently supported?

Supporting these resources requires more than awaiting the cached function. Streamlit would need defined behavior for:

- persistent event-loop ownership;
- ensuring resource operations execute on the owning loop;
- global versus session-scoped resources;
- async `validate` and `on_release` callback execution;
- cleanup when a cache, session, or server shuts down;
- thread safety and concurrent access;
- reconnects and reruns.

The common case—caching an inert value produced asynchronously—does not require this lifecycle machinery and is covered separately by #16168.

Users can currently avoid the problem by:

- creating, using, and closing the client within one coroutine invocation;
- caching the inert result rather than the client;
- using a synchronous client when one is available; or
- managing a dedicated long-lived event loop themselves.

Given these workarounds and currently limited evidence of demand, this is not planned as part of the initial async cache support.

### Feedback wanted

Please react with a thumbs-up and describe your use case if the workarounds are insufficient. In particular, it would help to know:

- which client or resource you need to cache;
- whether it should be shared globally or only within one session;
- why creating it per operation is impractical; and
- how you currently manage async execution in your Streamlit app.

### Relationship to rerun-resilient streaming

Rerun-resilient streaming is planned separately in #14524. That work addresses streams being interrupted by reruns and may resolve the specific `st.write_stream` workflow in #12076. This feature request covers the broader lifecycle problem of reusing cached event-loop-bound resources across reruns and APIs.

### Additional context

- General async cache request: #8308
- Example `Event loop is closed` failure: #12076
- Initial async cache implementation: #16168

title: Preserve coroutine-function detection for async cached functions
body:
## Summary

PR [#16168](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16168) adds async-aware `st.cache_data` and `st.cache_resource`. An async cached function remains awaitable, but the decorated object is a `CachedFunc` whose `__call__` is synchronous and returns an awaitable. As a result:

```python
import inspect

import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data
async def cached_lookup(query: str) -> str:
    return await search_service(query)


assert not inspect.iscoroutinefunction(cached_lookup)
result = cached_lookup("streamlit")
assert inspect.isawaitable(result)
value = await result
```

This issue is a searchable decision record and a place to collect demand for preserving coroutine-function detection through the cache decorators. It is not committed follow-up work and does not block #16168.

## Affected integrations

Some frameworks inspect a callback before invoking it to decide whether to use their sync or async execution path:

- LangChain `RunnableLambda`
- LlamaIndex `FunctionTool`
- MCP callback/tool registration, including decorator-based tool APIs
- Similar callback systems such as Gradio

When the decorated `CachedFunc` is classified as synchronous, a framework may invoke it on its sync path and treat the returned coroutine as the sync result instead of awaiting it.

## Supported compatibility pattern

Keep the cached implementation separate and pass a true `async def` adapter to APIs that inspect callbacks. This reusable adapter preserves coroutine-function detection while still calling through the cache:

```python
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from typing import ParamSpec, TypeVar

P = ParamSpec("P")
R = TypeVar("R")


def as_async_callback(
    cached_func: Callable[P, Awaitable[R]],
) -> Callable[P, Awaitable[R]]:
    async def callback(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
        return await cached_func(*args, **kwargs)

    return callback


retrieve_callback = as_async_callback(cached_lookup)

runnable = RunnableLambda(retrieve_callback)
tool = FunctionTool.from_defaults(fn=retrieve_callback)
```

For decorator-based MCP registration, keep the cached function separate from the registered tool:

```python
@st.cache_data
async def cached_customer(customer_id: int) -> dict:
    return await database.fetch(customer_id)


@mcp.tool()
async def lookup_customer(customer_id: int) -> dict:
    return await cached_customer(customer_id)
```

Do not use `inspect.unwrap(cached_lookup)` as the callback. It returns the original function and therefore bypasses Streamlit caching.

## Demand collection

Please comment if the async-adapter pattern cannot satisfy your use case. Include:

- the framework and version;
- how the callback is registered and invoked; and
- why a separate `async def` adapter is insufficient.

That evidence can inform whether Streamlit should preserve coroutine-function detection directly in a future change.

## Related

- [#16168](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16168) — async-aware cache decorators
- [#8308](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8308) — general async cached-function support

title: st.multiselect no longer inserts the first filtered option on Enter (works in 1.49.1, not in 1.62.0)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In `st.multiselect`, typing a few letters and pressing Enter used to insert the first filtered option. Since the react-aria migration it inserts nothing: no option is marked as the user types, so Enter has nothing to commit and simply closes the list.

`st.selectbox` still commits its first filtered option on Enter, which is why this reads as an oversight rather than a decision, but I may be wrong about that and would rather ask than assume.

Filing it because the same migration produced #16003 (fuzzy search became contiguous-substring matching), which was accepted as a regression, and this is the same shape of quiet behaviour loss.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

picked = st.multiselect("Multi", ["Person", "Organization", "Department", "Role", "Project"])
st.write("multiselect:", picked)

one = st.selectbox("Single", ["Person", "Organization", "Role"], index=None)
st.write("selectbox:", one)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click the multiselect and type `Pe`.
2. Press Enter.
3. Do the same in the selectbox below it.

### Expected Behavior

Enter inserts `Person`, the first filtered option, as it did in 1.49.1 and as the selectbox still does in 1.62.0.

### Current Behavior

Enter clears the text and closes the list, and nothing is selected.

Comparing the same script on both versions, in the DOM after typing `Pe`:

| | 1.49.1 | 1.62.0 |
|---|---|---|
| options offered | Person, Project, Department | same (the fuzzy filter is unchanged) |
| first option | `aria-selected="true"`, tinted row | nothing marked, no `aria-activedescendant` |
| Enter | inserts Person | inserts nothing |
| extra row | none | `Select N matches`, keyed `__select_matches__` |
| selectbox, Enter | - | inserts the first option |

The arrow keys reach the option, but the first ArrowDown lands on the new `Select N matches` row, so the natural keyboard recovery (ArrowDown, Enter) selects *every* match rather than the one that was wanted. It takes ArrowDown twice.

I could not find a prop in React Aria's ComboBox for list autocomplete with automatic selection, so I appreciate this may not be a small change. The WAI-ARIA APG lists both automatic and manual selection as valid patterns, so this is a design question as much as a bug, which is why the question is in the summary.

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (working in 1.49.1)
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

Related: #16003 and #15438 (the BaseWeb to react-aria migration).

title: [Bug] st.dataframe() / st.table() silently kill WebSocket when DataFrame has non-ASCII column names + emoji data (no traceback, session loss)
body:
## Summary

`st.dataframe()` and `st.table()` silently close the WebSocket connection when the DataFrame contains **non-ASCII column names** (e.g. `ç`, `ê`, `/`) **combined with emoji in cell data**. No Python exception is raised, no error appears in the terminal — the browser simply reconnects with a brand-new session, wiping `st.session_state` entirely.

This is one of the hardest bugs to debug in Streamlit because it produces **zero tracebacks** and presents itself as an unrelated UX problem ("users keep getting logged out").

---

## Versions

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| streamlit | 1.41.0 |
| pandas | 2.2.3 |
| Python | 3.11 |
| OS | Linux (Docker, python:3.11-slim) |

---

## Minimal Reproduction

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# This persists fine
if "logged_in" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["logged_in"] = False

if not st.session_state["logged_in"]:
    if st.button("Login"):
        st.session_state["logged_in"] = True
        st.rerun()
    st.stop()

st.write("✅ Logged in — session_state alive")

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Serviço": ["Manutenção Website", "Hospedagem"],   # ← non-ASCII column name (cedilha)
    "Valor/mês": ["R$ 100,00", "R$ 200,00"],           # ← non-ASCII + slash in column name  
    "Status": ["🟢 Ativo", "🔴 Pausado"],              # ← emoji in cell data
})

st.dataframe(df)   # 💥 WebSocket dies here — no exception raised
st.write("This line never renders — session is already dead")
```

Run with Docker:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install streamlit==1.41.0 pandas==2.2.3
COPY app.py .
ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "run", "app.py", "--server.headless=true", "--server.fileWatcherType=none"]
```

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Build and run the container
2. Open `http://localhost:8501`
3. Click "Login" → session is alive (`session_state["logged_in"] = True`)
4. `st.dataframe(df)` renders (or tries to)
5. Browser reconnects → `session_state` is empty → "Login" button appears again

---

## Observed Behavior

- `st.dataframe(df)` call executes without raising any Python exception
- The line after `st.dataframe()` **never executes** (confirmed via `print()` to stdout)
- Browser-side: WebSocket closes and immediately reconnects with a fresh session
- `st.session_state` is wiped clean — any auth/navigation state is lost
- **Identical behavior with `st.table(df)`** — same root cause

### Diagnostic method that revealed the bug

Since no traceback is produced, the only way to isolate it was:

1. Store a UUID in `session_state` on first load: `st.session_state["sid"] = uuid4()`
2. Display it on every render: `st.caption(f"sid: {st.session_state['sid']}")`
3. Add `print()` statements throughout the render function (visible in Docker logs)
4. The `print()` output stopped exactly at the `st.dataframe()` call
5. The displayed `sid` changed to a new value on the next render → confirmed new WebSocket session

---

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The bug appears to occur during **Arrow/protobuf serialization** of the DataFrame when:
- Column names contain multi-byte UTF-8 characters (`ç` = U+00E7, `ê` = U+00EA, `/` combined with accented chars)
- AND cell data contains 4-byte Unicode emoji (`🟢` = U+1F7E2, `🔴` = U+1F534)

The serialization fails at the **protocol level** (WebSocket frame), not at the Python level. The exception is caught internally by Streamlit/PyArrow and manifests as a connection close rather than an error message.

The bug does **not** occur when:
- Column names are ASCII-only
- Cell data has no emoji
- `st.write(df.to_dict(orient="records"))` is used instead (routes through JSON, not Arrow)

---

## Workaround

Replace `st.dataframe()` / `st.table()` with a **GFM markdown table** rendered via `st.markdown()`:

```python
def _esc(v) -> str:
    """Escape pipe to prevent breaking markdown table structure."""
    return str(v).replace("|", "\\|")

lines = [
    "| Servico | Valor_mes | Status |",
    "|---|---|---|",
]
for _, row in df.iterrows():
    lines.append(f"| {_esc(row['Serviço'])} | {_esc(row['Valor/mês'])} | {row['Status']} |")

st.markdown("\n".join(lines))
```

This bypasses the Arrow serialization layer entirely.

---

## Expected Behavior

- `st.dataframe()` should either render the DataFrame correctly OR raise a visible Python exception / display an in-app error
- The WebSocket connection should **never** be closed silently due to a data rendering issue
- If Arrow serialization fails, Streamlit should fall back to a JSON/HTML representation rather than terminating the session

---

## Additional Notes

- `fileWatcherType = "none"` was confirmed active — rules out hot-reload as the cause
- The Docker container did **not** restart (verified via log message count)
- The bug is **100% reproducible** in the described environment
- Changing column names to ASCII-only (`Servico`, `Valor_mes`) likely resolves the Arrow schema issue

Would appreciate confirmation of the root cause and whether a fix is planned for 1.41.x or 1.42.0.

title: Keyed `st.dataframe` / `st.data_editor` keep positional selection and edit state across a data change, so actions land on the wrong row
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary A keyed `st.dataframe` or `st.data_editor` excludes its data from the element identity: `key_as_main_identity={"selection_mode", "is_selection_activated"}` at [arrow.py lines 1280-1284](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/arrow.py#L1280-L1284). The element id therefore survives a data refresh, and the browser resends grid state that was computed against the previous frame. `event.selection.rows` and `edited_rows` are positional, so after a rerun that reorders or inserts rows those positions address different records, and the app receives a selection or an edit for a row the user never touched. There is no error and no warning. The comment directly above that call site acknowledges that selections "can become orphaned when the data changes" and that resetting them "might be a nice enhancement"; the effect on an app that acts on the selection is a wrong-row write, not a cosmetic orphan. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import pandas as pd import streamlit as st st.session_state.setdefault("gen", 0) st.session_state.setdefault("closed", []) # Simulates a queue whose contents change between reruns (a new ticket arrived). rows = ["TICK-101", "TICK-102", "TICK-103", "TICK-104"] if st.session_state["gen"]: rows = ["TICK-100", *rows] df = pd.DataFrame({"ticket": rows}) event = st.dataframe(df, key="queue", on_select="rerun", selection_mode="single-row") if st.button("Simulate new ticket arriving", key="refresh"): st.session_state["gen"] += 1 st.rerun() if st.button("Close selected", key="close") and event.selection.rows: position = event.selection.rows[0] st.session_state["closed"].append(df.iloc[position]["ticket"]) st.write("Selected positions:", event.selection.rows) st.write("Closed:", st.session_state["closed"]) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. `streamlit run` (or `uv run streamlit run`) the snippet. 2. Click the row showing `TICK-102` (position 1). The app shows `Selected positions: [1]`. 3. Click "Simulate new ticket arriving". `TICK-102` gets bumped down to position 2, but the highlighted row and `event.selection.rows` are still `[1]`, which is now `TICK-101`. 4. Click "Close selected". You get `Closed: ['TICK-101']` even though you had initially selected `TICK-102`. The same holds for `st.data_editor` with the default `num_rows="fixed"`: a pending `edited_rows` entry is re-applied at the same position after the frame changes. The identity part can be shown without a browser, using `AppTest`: ```python from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest def script(): import pandas as pd import streamlit as st st.session_state.setdefault("gen", 0) if st.button("refresh", key="refresh"): st.session_state["gen"] += 1 rows = ["TICK-101", "TICK-102", "TICK-103", "TICK-104"] if st.session_state["gen"]: rows = ["TICK-100", *rows] df = pd.DataFrame({"ticket": rows}) st.dataframe(df, key="queue", on_select="rerun", selection_mode="single-row") st.dataframe(df, on_select="rerun", selection_mode="single-row") at = AppTest.from_function(script).run() keyed, unkeyed = at.dataframe[0].proto.id, at.dataframe[1].proto.id at.button(key="refresh").click().run() print(keyed == at.dataframe[0].proto.id) # True -> keyed id survives the data change print(unkeyed == at.dataframe[1].proto.id) # False -> unkeyed id does not ``` ### Expected Behavior When the data behind a keyed grid changes, stale selection and edit state should be reset (or the state should be keyed by row identity rather than position), so an app never receives positions computed against a frame it is no longer showing. At minimum the docs for `key=` on `st.dataframe` / `st.data_editor` should say that selection and edit state is positional and survives data changes. ### Current Behavior Positional selection and edit state is preserved across data changes for keyed grids. Dropping `key=` makes the id data-dependent and the stale state orphans to empty, which is safe but discards every pending selection or edit on any data change, and contradicts the general advice to always give widgets a key. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. Not a recent regression, at least. The row retarget in steps 1-4 was observed in Chromium on 1.60.0. The `AppTest` demonstration above prints `True` / `False` on both 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (the latest release at the time of writing), and the identity code is unchanged at the current tip of `develop`. On 1.60.0 and later the `st.data_editor` case is wider than on 1.59.x: a keyed editor with `num_rows="fixed"` re-applies a pending edit at the same position after a reorder, where 1.59.x discarded it. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit - Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) ### Additional Information Related: `_apply_dataframe_edits` ([data_editor.py#L560-L564](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/data_editor.py#L560-L564)) receives no `disabled` argument, so `disabled=["_index"]` is enforced only in the browser; a client-sent index edit is applied server-side. Apps that act on grid state currently have to pin the frame they rendered in `st.session_state`, resolve positions against that frame, and reject anything they did not serve.

title: `heartbeat_ack` is discarded when a script run starts before the queue flushes
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`ForwardMsgQueue.clear(retain_lifecycle_msgs=True)` keeps only `new_session`, `script_finished`, `session_status_changed`, `parent_message`, `page_info_changed` and toast deltas ([forward_msg_queue.py lines 135-146](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/runtime/forward_msg_queue.py#L135-L146)). `heartbeat_ack` is not in that set, so an ack that is already sitting in the queue is destroyed instead of delivered. `AppSession._clear_queue` calls this on every `SCRIPT_STARTED`, and the runtime flushes queues on a short timer, so an ack enqueued in the window between a heartbeat arriving and the next script run starting never reaches the browser. A host that sends one `SEND_APP_HEARTBEAT` and waits for the ack can wait forever.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit.proto.ForwardMsg_pb2 import ForwardMsg
from streamlit.runtime.forward_msg_queue import ForwardMsgQueue

queue = ForwardMsgQueue()

ack = ForwardMsg()
ack.heartbeat_ack = True
finished = ForwardMsg()
finished.script_finished = ForwardMsg.FINISHED_SUCCESSFULLY

queue.enqueue(ack)
queue.enqueue(finished)
[m.WhichOneof("type") for m in queue._queue]  # ['heartbeat_ack', 'script_finished']

queue.clear(retain_lifecycle_msgs=True)
[m.WhichOneof("type") for m in queue._queue]  # ['script_finished']  <- ack is gone
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run` (or `uv run streamlit run`) the snippet.
2. Observe that the second print no longer contains `heartbeat_ack`.

End to end: open an app in an iframe host that sends `SEND_APP_HEARTBEAT` exactly once while a rerun is being triggered (for example, immediately after a widget interaction). The ack for that heartbeat is never received.

### Expected Behavior

A heartbeat ack is a one-shot reply to a client request, like a toast is a one-shot notification. It should survive the interrupted-run queue clear, or be sent directly rather than queued, so that one heartbeat always produces one ack.

### Current Behavior

The ack is silently removed from the queue when a script run starts before the queue is flushed. Nothing is logged. The client sees no reply.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced
- Python version: 3.14.6
- Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit
- Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) but **not browser-specific; reproduced as a pure function of `ForwardMsgQueue`**

### Additional Information

The toast case (#7740) was fixed by adding `_is_toast_delta(msg)` to the retain predicate ([forward_msg_queue.py line 146](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/runtime/forward_msg_queue.py#L146)); the same shape would fix this (`msg.WhichOneof("type") == "heartbeat_ack"`). We hit this from a test harness that uses a heartbeat round trip to prove a WebSocket reconnect completed; sending heartbeats on an interval rather than once is the workaround.

title: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If a default value is set in session state on one page run, and then subsequently a widget is rendered with a corresponding `key`, then the default value is not picked up properly and the frontend and backend show different values for that widget.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Sets default on first page run
st.session_state.setdefault("foo", 100.0)

if st.toggle("Show"):
    foo = st.number_input("Foo", key="foo")  # Shows 0.00
    st.write("You entered:", foo)  # Shows 100.0
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1.Turn on the  toggle
2. Compare the value in the widget vs the value printed underneath

### Expected Behavior

The value in the widget should match the number reported underneath.

### Current Behavior

The input widget displays `0.00`, but the backend reports `You entered: 100`.

If `r` is pressed to trigger a re-run, then the frontend updates to display `0.0` and the default value is lost.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

This bug is problematic for more complex pages, where widgets may need to be "loaded" or "reset" programmatically, and some widgets may be conditionally hidden depending on a toggle or checkbox.

The bug does not happen if `persist_state="page"` is passed to `number_input`.

Possibly related: #15660 seems to have fixed a similar bug for when persist_state is passed, but not for when persist_state=None.

import sys

_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX = "_counter_value"

def _render_button_in_dialog(page_key: str) -> None:

title: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

### Additional Information

Found during QA of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17106#issuecomment-5813147965.

Related:

- #3512 — unmount should reset both the widget UI and the Python value in the same run
- #17093 / #17106 — delayed first mount after a leftover pre-registration user key (out of scope here)
- #12880 — identity-by-key (out of scope)

title: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A Custom Components v2 (CCv2) `setTriggerValue` call is silently lost when its rerun request is still queued and another widget update arrives before the script runner picks it up: the `on_<event>_change` callback never runs and `result.<event>` is never set. `st.button` survives the identical sequence. With default settings this affects components inside `@st.fragment`, and with `runner.fastReruns = false` it also affects full-app reruns.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time

import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("log", [])

probe = st.components.v2.component(
    "trigger_probe",
    html="<button id='fire'>Fire component trigger</button>",
    js="""
export default function (component) {
  const { parentElement, setTriggerValue } = component;
  parentElement.querySelector("#fire").onclick = () => setTriggerValue("fired", Date.now());
}
""",
)


@st.fragment
def panel():
    # result.fired only exists for events with an on_<event>_change callback.
    result = probe(key="probe", on_fired_change=lambda: None)
    if result.fired:
        st.session_state.log.append("component trigger received")
    if st.button("st.button"):
        st.session_state.log.append("st.button click received")
    st.text_input("Other widget", key="other")
    st.write("Received:", st.session_state.log)
    time.sleep(5)  # a slow fragment, so the next requests queue up


panel()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run app.py` and wait for the first run to finish (about 5 s).
2. Click **Fire component trigger** while the app is idle. `Received:` shows `component trigger received`. This is the control.
3. Type `a` into **Other widget** and press Enter. The fragment reruns and sleeps for 5 s.
4. Within those 5 s, click **Fire component trigger**, then replace the text in **Other widget** with `b` and press Enter.
5. Wait for the fragment to finish.
6. Repeat steps 3–5, but click **st.button** instead of **Fire component trigger**.

### Expected Behavior

After step 5 the log gains a second `component trigger received`, the same way step 6 adds `st.button click received`.

### Current Behavior

After step 5 the log still holds only the control entry: the trigger fired in step 4 never reaches Python, although the text input's new value is applied. After step 6, `st.button click received` is appended as expected.

A full-app version of the script (the same body without `@st.fragment`) behaves the same way when started with `--runner.fastReruns false`.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0)
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: macOS 27.0
- Browser: Chromium 152

### Additional Information

**Why it happens.** `AppSession.request_rerun` stops the current runner and starts a new one only when `runner.fastReruns` is on and the request has no `fragment_id`. A widget-triggered fragment rerun (or any rerun when `fastReruns` is off) is handed to the existing `ScriptRunner`. A fragment rerun also does not preempt the running script (`_fragment_run_should_not_preempt_script`), so it waits in the queue. If a rerun request is already queued, `ScriptRequests.request_rerun` merges the two requests with `_coalesce_widget_states(old, new)`. That keeps the newer message's widget states and carries forward only `trigger_value` and `chat_input_value` from the older one.

A CCv2 trigger is a `json_trigger_value` on the component's synthetic aggregator ID (`$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<id>__events`). The frontend deletes trigger values once it has sent them, so the newer message never contains the trigger, and the merge drops it.

`string_trigger_value`, used by `st.menu_button` and `st.column_config.ButtonColumn`, is missing from the same list. Checking `_coalesce_widget_states` directly on 1.64.0, with a queued trigger of each type followed by a newer message for another widget:

| Queued trigger type | Kept after the merge |
|---|---|
| `trigger_value` (`st.button`) | yes |
| `chat_input_value` (`st.chat_input`) | yes |
| `string_trigger_value` (`st.menu_button`, `ButtonColumn`) | no |
| `json_trigger_value` (CCv2 `setTriggerValue`) | no |

I reproduced the CCv2 case in the browser. The `string_trigger_value` row is from the function-level check only.

**Suggested fix.** 1.64.0 already has `_TRIGGER_PROTO_FIELDS` and `_has_active_trigger_value`, and `_coalesce_replay_trigger_states` uses them. `_coalesce_widget_states` could apply its existing carry-forward rule to every active trigger type through the same helper, instead of the hard-coded two-item list. When both messages carry a `json_trigger_value` for the same aggregator ID, concatenating the two event lists would keep both events. A rough sketch:

```python
import json  # not imported in script_requests.py today


def _trigger_events(state):
    events = json.loads(state.json_trigger_value)
    return events if isinstance(events, list) else [events]


# In _coalesce_widget_states, replacing the loop over the two-item list:
for old_state in old_states.widgets:
    if not _has_active_trigger_value(old_state):
        continue
    trigger_type = old_state.WhichOneof("value")
    new_state = states_by_id.get(old_state.id)
    if new_state is None or (
        new_state.WhichOneof("value") == trigger_type
        and not _has_active_trigger_value(new_state)
    ):
        # Today's rule, applied to every trigger type.
        states_by_id[old_state.id] = old_state
    elif trigger_type == "json_trigger_value" == new_state.WhichOneof("value"):
        # Both messages carry CCv2 events for one aggregator: keep both lists.
        merged = WidgetState()
        merged.CopyFrom(new_state)
        merged.json_trigger_value = json.dumps(_trigger_events(old_state) + _trigger_events(new_state))
        states_by_id[old_state.id] = merged
```

With this patched in at startup on 1.64.0, the browser repro above passes: the trigger fired in step 4 reaches Python, and the text input's new value is applied too. At the function level it keeps all four trigger types from the table and merges two events sent to one aggregator into a single list.

**Related.** The automated triage comment on #16732 (mount-time `setTriggerValue` dropped) noted this gap. The fix that closed it, #16833, made one non-test change, to `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive` in the frontend, so this backend path is unchanged. #16765 added the replay-trigger helpers that the fix above could reuse. The tech spec in the open spec PR #16763 (session-owned rerun mailbox) lists all four trigger types as ones that "may not be dropped by coalescing" and calls this the carry-forward already implemented. In 1.64.0, `_coalesce_widget_states` carries two of them. The same two-item list is on `develop` as of 2026-10-01 and in 1.52.0, so this is not a regression.

title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

AppTest loses a conditional text input's value when it is hidden and shown again with `persist_state="page"`, although the test never switches pages. The same sequence retains the value in a browser, and `persist_state="session"` works in AppTest.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Show", key="show"):
    st.text_input("SKU", key="sku", persist_state="page")
""").run()

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
at.text_input[0].set_value("SKU-42").run()
at.toggle[0].set_value(False).run()
print("While hidden:", repr(at.session_state["sku"]))
assert at.session_state["sku"] == "SKU-42"

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
print("After showing again:", repr(at.text_input[0].value))
assert not at.exception
assert at.text_input[0].value == "SKU-42"  # Fails: actual value is "".
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Streamlit 1.65.0 in a normal Python environment: `pip install streamlit==1.65.0`.
2. Save the example as `repro_page_persistence.py` and run `python repro_page_persistence.py`. Pytest is not required.
3. Observe that the hidden value is still `SKU-42`, but the final input value is empty and the final assertion fails.
4. Change `persist_state="page"` to `persist_state="session"` and run again. The value remains `SKU-42` and the assertion passes.
5. For a browser comparison, save only the app string as `app.py`, run `streamlit run app.py`, enable Show, enter `SKU-42` and press Enter, then disable and re-enable Show. The browser retains the input value.

### Expected Behavior

Page-scoped persistence should keep the value through the hide/show sequence in AppTest because the test remains on the same page. It should return `SKU-42` after the input is shown again, matching the browser.

### Current Behavior

Reproduced on both Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0:

```text
While hidden: 'SKU-42'
After showing again: ''
AssertionError
```

There are no application exceptions in `at.exception`; the failure is the final test assertion. A browser comparison on both versions retains `SKU-42`. AppTest's `persist_state="session"` control also retains it; the default `persist_state=None` control resets it as expected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

A previously working version has not been established. The versions tested are 1.64.0 and 1.65.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0; also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python version: 3.14.8.
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest reproduction. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS.
- Package integrity: The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes. No installed Streamlit source was modified.

### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) concerns the remount of a `persist_state=None` widget and a backend/frontend mismatch. This reproduction uses explicit page persistence and works in a browser.
- [#17093](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17093) concerns a delayed first mount after a session-state value was set. Here, the widget was mounted, edited, hidden, and remounted.
- [#16611](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16611) concerns `AppTest.switch_page()` with a custom `url_path`. This example has no page switch or custom URL path.
- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) and [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) report KeyErrors with changing widget trees. This example has no script exception and loses a page-persistent value.

I did not find an existing issue with this same reproduction.

#### Possible cause

AppTest creates a fresh PagesManager for each run. Its current page hash initially equals `""`. ScriptRunner interprets the mismatch with the target page hash as a page change and performs cleanup before resetting the context, so page-scoped persistence can be evaluated against the empty current hash.

Source links are pinned to the inspected develop commit `ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e`:

- [AppTest creates PagesManager](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L506).
- [PagesManager initializes an empty current page hash](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/pages_manager.py#L50).
- [ScriptRunner performs page-change cleanup before context reset](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L660).

In a separate single-page diagnostic on both released versions, seeding the reconstructed runner's current page hash with the main page hash before cleanup makes this reproduction pass. It also prevents a keyed stateful tab from resetting after a child-widget interaction in AppTest. This diagnostic is evidence about the cleanup path; a complete fix must still handle real page switches correctly. The develop source was inspected, not executed.
